result.reason: Clarity: A uses plain-language headings (how it performed / what we changed / fee change) and glosses its own jargon — the benchmark is explained as global stocks and US bonds at glide path target weights, and the fee change is tied to the parents' own May request. B is four dense paragraphs, cites the comparison index without saying what it is, leaves 'breakpoint purposes' unexplained, and says 'our cash position,' which blurs ownership of the account. Tone: the tone notes require a direct answer to Nils's question about 70% equities with five years to college. A answers it — names Nils, explains the target steps down automatically each year, and reassures that the first-year tuition money is out of the market and in maturity-matched 2031 Treasuries. B merely notes the adjustment 'aligns with your question,' acknowledging the concern without resolving it. B is also more boilerplate ('We are pleased to share,' 'discuss your financial goals further'), frames a client-requested fee cut as firm good news, and 'your son Mateo' reads distant. A's warmth and open invitation to call suit parents planning for a 13-year-old. Length was not a factor; A's additional text is doing the specific job of answering the household's question.
